soc: Snapdragon 8 Gen 1 (India & Brazil; Exynos 2200 in Europe)
notes: Feb 2022. First Galaxy S generation where BOTH India and Brazil/South America officially received the Snapdragon variant (8 Gen 1) instead of Exynos (Americas = Snapdragon per GSMArena regional breakdown). India launch Rs 72,999. Final major update Android 16 / One UI 8 (rolled out Oct 2025; excluded from One UI 8.5 — confirmed end of major OS support). Discontinued.
caveats: IN/BR retail units are Snapdragon (SM-S901E) — in-house tested fine (ground truth). WARNING: EU Exynos 2200 units (SM-S901B, codename r0s) circulate as grey imports in India and have in-house-verified HEVC encoder timestamp instability — compat-check must distinguish by SoC/encoder name (c2.exynos vs c2.qti), not model name. Samsung exposes the ultrawide both as a separate public camera ID and (on newer One UI) via sub-1.0 zoom on the logical back camera; the zoom-ratio path was exercised in in-house testing on this model. Snapdragon 8 Gen 1 runs hot generally, but 1080p30 HEVC capture passed in-house.

notes: Feb 2022. India launch Rs 84,999. Snapdragon in both target markets. Final OS Android 16 / One UI 8 (no One UI 8.5). Discontinued.
caveats: Same SoC, camera HAL and 120-degree UW module as the in-house-verified base S22 (Snapdragon); larger body should dissipate heat at least as well, but this exact model was not bench-tested — thermal marked likely. Same grey-import warning as base S22: EU Exynos 2200 units (SM-S906B) have HEVC encoder timestamp instability; gate by SoC at runtime.

notes: Feb 2022. Merged the Note line (S Pen in body). India launch Rs 1,09,999. Only S22-series model with AF on the ultrawide (confirmed). Final OS Android 16 / One UI 8 (no One UI 8.5). Discontinued.
caveats: Same SoC/HAL family as in-house-verified S22 (Snapdragon); not individually bench-tested, thermal marked likely (largest body of the trio, best dissipation). UW has dual-pixel AF — app drives AF off + fixed focus, verify fixed-focus behaves on the AF-capable UW module during QA. Grey-import Exynos (SM-S908B) carries the HEVC timestamp-instability flag; gate by SoC at runtime.

soc: Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 for Galaxy (worldwide, incl. IN & BR)
notes: Feb 2023. First all-Snapdragon global S generation — no Exynos variant exists. India launch Rs 74,999. Currently on Android 16 / One UI 8; entitled to one more major update (Android 17). Mostly cleared out of official channels by mid-2026.
caveats: All-Snapdragon generation removes the Exynos grey-import risk entirely. Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 encoder (c2.qti.hevc.encoder) is in the reliable bucket (documented CBR support, timestamp-driven rate control). ARCore certified; flagship-tier REALTIME timestamp source expected. Not in-house tested — UW reach via zoom-ratio inferred from the verified S22 sibling + newer One UI exposing sub-1.0 zoom on logical ID 0; runtime probe remains decisive. 8 Gen 2 thermals much improved over 8 Gen 1.

notes: Feb 2023. India launch Rs 94,999. Discontinued/clearance by mid-2026. One more major update (Android 17) due.
caveats: Identical platform to Galaxy S23 (Snapdragon 8 Gen 2, same 120-degree UW module, ARCore certified). Not in-house tested; thermal likely (larger body than base S23).

notes: Feb 2023. 200 MP main. India launch Rs 1,24,999. Currently Android 16 / One UI 8, one major update remaining. Mostly out of official stock mid-2026.
caveats: Same Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 platform; ARCore certified. UW has dual-pixel AF — verify the app's AF-off + fixed-focus path on the AF-capable UW module during QA (same note as S22 Ultra). Not in-house tested; thermal likely.

soc: Exynos 2200 (India & Brazil; Snapdragon 8 Gen 1 in US)
notes: Oct 2023. India launch Rs 59,999; Brazil launch Oct 27, 2023 at R$ 3.999 (128 GB) / R$ 4.499 (256 GB), Exynos 2200 confirmed for the Brazilian and Indian units (global SM-S711B = Exynos 2200; only North America got Snapdragon 8 Gen 1). Currently Android 16 / One UI 8.
caveats: CRITICAL: the IN/BR variant runs the Exynos 2200 — the exact SoC whose HEVC encoder showed timestamp instability in in-house Galaxy S22 (Exynos) testing. Encoder gate cannot be trusted from spec sheet; expect possible fps-gate cancels or drift-telemetry degradation until bench-tested. Exynos rate control also ignores frame timestamps (WebRTC forces FRAMERATE_ADJUSTMENT for Exynos encoders). Thermal unknown: Exynos 2200 has a poor sustained-load reputation and no in-house 25-min capture data exists. UW FOV 123 degrees is a comfortable spec pass and ARCore certification covers the IMU/timestamp gates, but this device must NOT be promoted above Unverified without hardware testing. US Snapdragon variant (r11q) would likely fare better but is not sold in IN/BR.

soc: Exynos 2400 (India & Brazil; Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 only US/Canada/China/Taiwan/Hong Kong)
notes: Jan 2024. 7-year OS/security promise (to Android 21). Both India and Brazil sell the Exynos 2400 variant (SM-S921B confirmed Exynos for India; Snapdragon regions corrected from input's 'US/CA/CN/JP' to US/Canada/China/Taiwan/Hong Kong). A Snapdragon SM-S921E for India surfaced post-launch but the mainline retail unit is Exynos. Currently Android 16 / One UI 8. Street prices approximate — heavy discounting since S25/S26 launches.
caveats: IN/BR variant is Exynos 2400 — encoder behavior has little public data (mixed/unknown bucket): no in-house negative evidence like the 2200, but the Exynos encoder lineage ignores frame timestamps for rate control and CBR support must be verified via isBitrateModeSupported(CBR) at runtime. Everything else is strong: 120-degree UW, ARCore certified, S24-generation One UI exposes sub-1.0 zoom on the logical back camera to third parties. Thermals on the 2400 are much improved over the 2200. Promote to Supported only after an Exynos 2400 unit passes a bench capture.

notes: Jan 2024. India launch Rs 99,999. QHD+ display vs base S24. Mostly cleared from official stock by mid-2026; 7-year update promise.
caveats: Identical platform to Galaxy S24 (Exynos 2400 in IN/BR): encoder gate unverifiable from public data — runtime CBR check required; one bench-tested Exynos 2400 device would clear the whole S24/S24+/S24 FE group. ARCore certified; 120-degree UW; larger body than base S24 helps thermals.

soc: Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 for Galaxy (worldwide, incl. IN & BR)
notes: Jan 2024. Titanium frame, 200 MP main. Snapdragon worldwide (unlike base/Plus). India launch Rs 1,29,999. Currently Android 16 / One UI 8; 7-year update promise.
caveats: Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 worldwide — no Exynos variant of the Ultra exists, so no grey-import SoC ambiguity. Reliable Qualcomm encoder bucket; ARCore certified; S24-generation third-party zoom-out to UW confirmed working on newer One UI. UW has dual-pixel AF — verify fixed-focus path in QA. Not in-house tested; thermal likely (8 Gen 3 efficient, large vapor chamber).

notes: Oct 2024. Single global SoC (Exynos 2400e — slightly downclocked 2400). 7-year update promise; currently Android 16 / One UI 8. Street prices approximate after S25 FE launch.
caveats: Exynos 2400e everywhere (no Snapdragon variant) — same encoder uncertainty as S24/S24+: little public data on c2.exynos.hevc.encoder CBR/timestamp behavior on the 2400 generation; runtime isBitrateModeSupported(CBR) check required. 123-degree UW is a comfortable FOV pass; ARCore certified (FE variants included). Strong price-fit for the Rs 30K+ target band, which makes bench-testing one Exynos 2400-family unit worthwhile before promoting the group.

soc: Snapdragon 8 Elite for Galaxy (worldwide, incl. IN & BR)
